newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Eight dead, 40,000 homeless in Honduras floods.
newsitem.headline: Eight dead, 40,000 homeless in Honduras floods.

text.p: At least eight people have been killed and up to 40,000 left homeless by heavy rains and flooding in northern Honduras, officials said on Wednesday.
Eleven consecutive days of tropical rains caused rivers to swell and flood the remote northern part of Honduras, one of the poorest countries in the hemisphere.
An overflowing river flooded nearly all of La Lima, a poor suburb of the country's second city of San Pedro Sula, some 160 km (100 miles) north of the capital Tegucigalpa, officials said.
"About 80 percent of the town has been affected by the flooding," Luis Velasquez, head of Honduras' Regional Emergency Committee, told Reuters.
The head of Honduras' Congress, Carlos Flores, visited the area on Wednesday and promised $200,000 in emergency aid.
Relief workers said many of the homeless had already been taken to emergency shelters in San Pedro Sula.
"It's sad to see our compatriots suffering this way," Flores told reporters during his visit.
President Carlos Roberto Reina was slated to visit the area later on Wednesday.
Radio stations in the capital asked residents to donate food and clothing to families forced from their homes by the rains.
Officials said they had not yet estimated how much damage had been done to the area and its important banana plantations.
